title: PRD: Cohesive Endpoint Behavior Profiles for Hosted Gen+Embed Bundles — Scope Freeze & Launch Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers building LLM features cite inconsistent behavior across our generation, chat, embeddings and rerank endpoints when switching model variants or during degradation (fallbacks). This PRD defines a minimal, testable set of behavioral profiles (determinism bounds, truncation/stop interplay, embedding vector stability, rerank score semantics) and a slim launch playbook so we ship a predictable hosted API surface for our initial gen+embed bundle. Goal: freeze a bounded set of behavioral guarantees for GA that are measurable in telemetry and covered by automated acceptance tests and evals. Out of scope for this launch: advanced per-tenant overrides, multi-turn KV persistence beyond session-level caching, and new tool-calling surface iterations.
acceptance_criteria: API contract: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank must return documented fields and error codes; sample payloads included in spec and validated by integration tests
Behavioral contracts: top-level guarantees (determinism band, stop-token handling, prefix caching semantics) are codified and implementable by runtime team

Regression harness: for each endpoint we have an eval suite with 200 canonical prompts (gen+chat) and 500 embedding pairs for cosine stability; nightly runs must report no >5% regression on key metrics without an approved exception
Fallbacks: when preferred model unavailable, routing rules must select compatible variant with documented cost/latency tradeoffs; canary fallback path tested in staging with synthetic traffic
SLOs and telemetry: 99th percentile latency and token-per-second metrics emit per-route, per-model tags; dashboards for launch must be configured and smoke gated
SDK parity: official JS/Python SDKs return identical contract fields for these endpoints and pass client-side conformance tests
Security/compliance: KMS integration for private tenants enabled for all endpoints; security review signed off and noted in release artifacts
Launch rollout: staged canary with 1% -> 10% -> 50% traffic slices and automated rollback on quality or availability alerts defined in runbook
launch_checklist: Finalize PRD and publish Confluence page with example payloads
Runtime: implement behavior contracts and provide performance profile for each model variant
Engineering: unit/integration tests + regression harness merged to main (ENG-40234, ENG-45121)
Console: per-route dashboard templates created and linked in runbook
SDKs: JS/Python release candidate with conformance test badges
Documentation: API reference, quickstarts, and migration notes published
Security: KMS config documented; compliance checklist completed
Canary plan: traffic slices and success/failure criteria encoded in rollout config
Support: customer-facing changelog drafted and CS/SE briefing scheduled
Monitoring: alert rules for latency, error rate, quality regression, and fallback frequency enabled
Chaos test: simulate model outage during canary and validate automatic fallback behavior
Go/no-go: cross-functional readiness review (PM, Eng, Design, Security, SRE) 48 hours before cutover
decisions: Ship a single behavioral profile per endpoint family (gen/chat, embeddings, rerank) rather than per-model guarantees to reduce complexity
Scope freeze: include prefix/KV cache semantics for session-level only; persistent long-term KV is out of scope
Determinism contract: document a determinism band (measured variance) rather than absolute deterministic output; customers can request stronger guarantees as enterprise add-on
Fallback hierarchy: prefer quantized or smaller-family variants in-region before cross-region failover to preserve latency SLAs
scope_changes: Removed: per-tenant custom stop-token behavior for GA (deprioritized)
Added: embedding cosine-stability checks and a small canonical anchor dataset for regression detection
Clarified: rerank score normalization format to be an explicit float in [0,1] with tie-breaking rules
notes: Counterproposal evaluated: per-model SLAs were rejected due to operational surface area increase
PM to run two stakeholder workshops (SRE, Security, Platform) during Cycle 2026-W09 to align rollout criteria
Plan includes an emergency rollback play that re-routes gen requests to degraded model family with explicit customer notices
